title: Managed-catalog tests inherit the caller's problem-path override
reasoning: The override tests explicitly establish that SCBENCH_PROBLEMS_PATH takes precedence over the supplied managed home and bypasses synchronization. However, the bootstrap and managed resume tests do not clear that environment variable. When a developer runs pytest with a valid local problem override configured, these tests exercise the override branch instead of their temporary managed installation, causing incorrect failures.
reproduction: Set SCBENCH_PROBLEMS_PATH to a valid flat problem directory and run test_ensure_catalog_installed_bootstraps_and_recovers_partial_install. Its expected fake_sync calls are bypassed by the documented override behavior.
recommendation: Add an autouse fixture that removes SCBENCH_PROBLEMS_PATH with monkeypatch before each catalog test; allow override-specific tests to set their own temporary value.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Override scenarios set the variable explicitly, but managed-catalog scenarios assume it was absent before pytest started. Monkeypatch restores the caller's environment after each override test.
suggestedRegressionTest: Run the catalog module with an externally configured valid override and verify that managed scenarios remain isolated while explicit override scenarios still pass.
